messages.author: 50376cb8eda8eca6
messages.subject: On using WAIC / LOO
parts:
Hi Paul,

A quick (and potentially silly) question - is it appropriate to use WAIC and/or LOO to compare models built using different families? For example, I have used the same data for models that use the gaussian, cumulative (logit), and cumulative (probit).


Thanks,
Paul

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] On using WAIC / LOO
parts: That is not a silly question at all. As long as the families are either both continuous or both discrete, comparisons are possible. If one is continuous and one is discrete, I believe things are more complicated, since the continuous likelhood does not capture probabilities itself, while the discrete likelihood does. Maybe you could also ask this question on http://discourse.mc-stan.org/?

messages.author: a236d3d356ca53fd
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] On using WAIC / LOO
parts:
Not a silly question. I've seen too many times someone not thinking about this all and making faulty comparison.
Paul is correct that you can't mix continuous and discrete. Coincidentally I did answer the continuous part in Stan discourse few weeks
ago with some explanation also what to do if comparing models for different transformations of http://discourse.mc-stan.org/t/model-comparison-via-psis-loo-for-3-level-hierarchical-growth-model/2905/2
You could also compare continuous and discrete if you discretize the continuous case by computing probabilities by integrating over intervals.

http://discourse.mc-stan.org/ is the best forum for asking questions related to loo package (which brms is also using for LOO and WAIC)
If you have further questions on this, please continue there.

Aki
